statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.498A, s.109 read with s.34 (FIR originally under s.307, converted to s.302)
evidence_type: Dying declaration (primary); medical evidence (post-mortem); Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate and investigating officer testimony; partial support from hostile witnesses
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged in dying declaration: beatings under influence of liquor and demands for money for a car; court did not separately weigh these as aggravating
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted both accused (benefit of doubt; dying declaration held not safe to rely upon)
high_court_outcome: Conviction of Krishan upheld by reversing acquittal; acquittal of mother Shardi maintained
offence_finally_established: Murder (causing death of wife by burning); specific sections of conviction not separately stated in judgment
neutral_facts: The victim was admitted to a hospital with serious burn injuries after a fire at the matrimonial home. The investigating police officer obtained a doctor's endorsement that the victim was fit to make a statement. A Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate then recorded the victim's statement at the hospital in question-and-answer form, and the victim's thumb impression was taken on it and identified by the investigating officer. In the statement the victim said that the accused, the victim's husband, had often beaten the victim while under the influence of liquor and had demanded money from the victim's father to buy a car. The victim said that on the morning of the incident the accused poured kerosene oil on the victim's body and set it on fire, and that the victim's father-in-law and sister-in-law came and helped put out the fire. The accused's mother was said to have instigated the accused. The victim died a few days later. The post-mortem examination found superficial to deep burns covering about 75 per cent of the body, sparing the lower thighs, legs and feet, and concluded that the burns were ante-mortem and sufficient to cause death. The victim's father, mother and sister were examined at trial but did not fully support the prosecution. The father said the accused had demanded money for a vehicle and that he had refused. The mother said the victim was never harassed for dowry. The sister of the accused said the victim caught fire while preparing tea and that the accused was not at home. The investigating officer, the magistrate and other police witnesses gave evidence on the recording of the statement and the investigation.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from burns (about 75% of body surface, superficial to deep); burns ante-mortem and sufficient to cause death
number_of_offences: 3 charged (ss.302, 498A, 109 read with s.34); conviction upheld, sections of conviction not separately stated
motive: alleged: demands for money to buy a car from the victim's father, and beatings by the accused under influence of liquor (as stated in dying declaration; court did not separately decide motive)
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declaration (Ex. PR/2) recorded by SDJM after doctor's fitness endorsement; post-mortem findings of PW14; partial support from PW1, PW9, PW11, PW14, SDJM and other police witnesses
witness_credibility: Hostile witnesses PW1, PW3 and PW4 held not to undermine the dying declaration; their evidence relied on only to the extent it supports the prosecution (e.g. PW1 on car money demand); doctor's cross-examination answer on burnt thumb held to offer no advantage to defence
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR registered 30 March 1998; victim died 2 April 1998); trial judgment: 15 November 1999; High Court: 17 July 2007; Supreme Court: 13 December 2012
legal_representation: Accused/appellant: Ram Naresh Yadav and Dr. Kailash Chand; State/respondent: Kamal Mohan Gupta, Mohd. Zahid Hussain and Sanjeev Kumar
investigation_status: FIR registered 30 March 1998 on dying declaration, later amended to s.302 after death; site plan, inquest and post-mortem conducted; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted both accused. High Court: convicted Krishan, maintained acquittal of Shardi. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld
prosecution_argument: Dying declaration can be relied upon without corroboration if true; hostility of witnesses does not defeat it (State relied on Ram Sagar Yadav)
defence_argument: Dying declaration unsafe as sole basis without corroboration (Khushal Rao); doctor's answer that both hands were burnt including thumb meant thumb impression could not have been taken; hostile witnesses leave prosecution case unproved
legal_principle_applied: A dying declaration can be the sole basis of conviction if true, reliable and recorded per established practice; hostility of witnesses is relevant but not determinative
precedent_relied_upon: Khushal Rao v. State of Bombay AIR 1958 SC 22; State of UP v. Ram Sagar Yadav (1985) 1 SCC 552; Munnu Raja v. State of MP (1976) 3 SCC 104; Ramilaben Hasmukhbhai Khristi v. State of Gujarat (2002) 7 SCC 56; Bhajju @ Karan Singh v. State of MP (2012) 4 SCC 327; Mrinal Das v. State of Tripura (2011) 9 SCC 479
